en.title: Smallest Missing Positive Integer After Choosing per Position
en.description:
At each position choose either A[i] or B[i] to form C, so that the smallest missing positive integer of C is as small as possible. This site judges by "minimize the missing value"; the original site described it as a number that cannot appear in any C, which contradicts its examples.

The input protocol, the ranges added by this site, the examples, and the tests were written independently by CSWork.
en.input: The first line contains N (1..100000), the second line contains A, and the third line contains B, each with N integers in 1..100000.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation:
Example 1: 1 and 3 are forced to appear by fixed positions, while 2 can be avoided; the answer is 2.

Example 2: 1 and 2 are forced to appear, and 3 can be avoided at every position; the answer is 3.

Example 3: the two positions can only pick 1 and 2, so the smallest missing number is 3.
hints: Only a position with A[i]=B[i] forces a value to appear. Collect these forced values and output the smallest positive integer not in that set.
